title: asq Office service envelopes
description: Contract revision 1.4 shared building blocks for every read that leaves the local process: ServiceStatus, ServiceError, the ServiceResult envelope and the Page/PageCoverage pair (backend-v1.4.md §3). This file owns no route of its own; the domain schemas (team-os.json, explainability.json, praxis.json, project-context.json) spell the envelope out again around their own typed data, and tools/test/contract-v14.test.mjs asserts every one of them repeats it field for field. Nothing here is ever the body of a local v1.3 read: §5 of data-contract.md keeps owning local errors, and backend-v1.4.md §7 documents the translation between the two.

Timestamp.description: UTC RFC3339 with an offset, as in data-contract.md §1. Time that is not established is null — never an empty string and never zero.

NullableTimestamp.description: A Timestamp or null. Null means the back-end never established the time, not that it is zero or unknown-but-recent.

ServiceStatus.description: Availability of the service that answered, and nothing else. Domain states — a run still processing, an agent not joined to a workspace, an insight with no recorded injection — are fields of the typed data model, never new members here (SHARED.md, new response models).

ServiceErrorCode.description: Finite. A ServiceError never carries an upstream code verbatim; the adapter maps to one of these and puts the bounded human sentence in detail.

ServiceError.title: ServiceError

detail.description: One sanitised, bounded sentence safe to show. Never a stack trace, a credential, a filesystem path, a raw upstream body or a URL carrying a key.

retryable.description: Whether an identical read may be repeated. An uncertain mutation outcome is never retryable here; see operation.json.

ServiceError.description: Why a service read did not produce data. Distinct from error.json, which stays the body of a non-2xx local /api response.

PageCoverage.title: PageCoverage

reported_total.description: What the upstream itself reported as the total. Null when it reported none — the back-end never counts a total the source did not establish.

total_is_exact.description: Whether reported_total is exact rather than an estimate or a lower bound. Null when reported_total is null.

failed_scope_count.description: Scopes that were asked and failed. Greater than zero is what makes Page.partial true.

omitted_scope_count.description: Scopes deliberately not asked (unconfigured, out of the resolved profile). Not a failure.

PageCoverage.description: The fixed coverage object. Every field is nullable because an upstream that establishes none of them must not be made to look precise; no adapter may add a field here.

Cursor.description: Opaque, bound to the query, profile and workspace that produced it. A cursor can only continue the page it came from: it never widens or changes scope, and one presented against a different query/profile/workspace is rejected with invalid (400).

Page.title: Page

items.description: The typed rows. Each concrete Page repeats this envelope with its own items schema; this generic form is documentation, not a body any route returns.

partial.description: True when at least one scope failed, so the page is known to be incomplete. Not the same as having a next_cursor, which only means more rows follow.

coverage.description: Null when the upstream establishes no coverage at all.

Page.description: Page<T> from SHARED.md. Bounded pagination defaults and maxima are in backend-v1.4.md §5.

ServiceResult.title: ServiceResult

data.description: The typed payload, or null. Null is explicit and always present as a key. Each concrete result repeats this envelope with its own data schema.

stale.description: True when data is a previously observed value rather than one read now. Only status ok or partial may carry stale data.

observed_at.description: When the data in this envelope was observed. Null when data is null.

last_success_at.description: The last time this service answered successfully at all, even if this read did not. Null when it never has.

error.description: Null exactly when status is ok.

ServiceResult.description: ServiceResult<T> from SHARED.md. Two invariants the schema cannot express and tools/test/contract-v14.test.mjs enforces instead: status ok has a non-null data and a null error, and unauthorized/forbidden/unconfigured always carry data null with stale false — losing authorisation must drop the cached body, never display a previously authorised one.
